q: The Preamble begins with 'We, the people of India'. This means the ultimate source of authority is
e: The Preamble declares the people as the source of the Constitution's authority.

q: The Constitution of India was adopted on
e: Adopted on 26 November 1949; it came into force on 26 January 1950.

q: Who chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
e: Ambedkar chaired the seven-member Drafting Committee.

q: The words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' were added to the Preamble by the
e: The 42nd Amendment (1976) is often called the mini-Constitution.

q: Article 14 guarantees
o: Equality before law and equal protection of laws
e: Article 14 is the foundation of the Right to Equality (Articles 14 to 18).

q: Dr. Ambedkar called this Article the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution
e: Article 32 gives the Right to Constitutional Remedies.

q: Article 21 protects the
o: Right to life and personal liberty
e: The Supreme Court has read dignity, privacy and livelihood into Article 21.

q: The Fundamental Duties are listed in
e: Added by the 42nd Amendment; there are 11 duties today.

q: The Directive Principles of State Policy are
e: Part IV of the Constitution; fundamental in governance but not justiciable.

q: The anti-defection law is contained in the
e: Added by the 52nd Amendment in 1985.

q: The voting age was lowered from 21 to 18 by the
e: The 61st Amendment (1989) amended Article 326.

q: Panchayati Raj institutions got constitutional status through the
e: The 73rd Amendment (1992) added Part IX.

q: The Right to Education (Article 21A) was added by the
e: Free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14.

q: The Goods and Services Tax was introduced by the
e: The 101st Amendment (2016) enabled GST.

q: The 10 percent reservation for Economically Weaker Sections came via the
e: The 103rd Amendment (2019) added Articles 15(6) and 16(6).

q: One-third reservation for women in legislatures was provided by the
e: The 106th Amendment (2023), to take effect after delimitation.

q: The Constitution originally had how many Schedules?
e: It began with 8 Schedules; there are 12 today.

q: The Union, State and Concurrent Lists are in the
e: The Seventh Schedule distributes legislative subjects.

q: The procedure for amending the Constitution is laid down in
e: Article 368 provides for three types of amendment.

q: Article 17 deals with the
e: Untouchability is abolished and its practice forbidden.
